prompt: Create one square, tileable base-color texture of an ordinary painted plaster wall for a Korean residential corridor. Reference image 1 is the CURRENT coarse unfinished plaster texture that reads incorrectly in the game: replace its busy swirled trowel ridges and mottled concrete blotches with the very quiet surface of plaster coated in several coats of warm off-white matte interior paint. Reference image 2 is an actual Korean residential lobby for the everyday maintained utility-building context, not for copying its stone aggregate. The output is only an orthographic flat albedo texture, representing a 180 cm square of wall, seamless on all four edges. Warm neutral pale grey white, approximate RGB 191,190,180, with extremely subtle fine roller stipple and very low-contrast irregular paint coverage. The paint covers the trowel scratches. No coarse pits, no raised islands, no mould, no cracks, no fake dirt border, no vignette, no baked shadows, no illumination gradient, no specular highlight, no bricks, no panels, no text, no objects. This is the calm large surface behind small readable props, not a dramatic decorative texture. Preserve barely perceptible natural paint grain at close range, nearly uniform tone at several metres. Output a single 1024x1024 image filling the canvas.
